title: How does Ledger validation work on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of Ledger validation and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, a closed XRPL ledger becomes final for a client when the client can establish that trusted validators have validated it. [1]

A proposed transaction, a server's preliminary result and a closed ledger are distinct stages. Consensus determines the agreed transaction set and deterministic execution produces ledger state. Applications should use validated results and the transaction's actual outcome before delivering paid goods. Validation authenticates the ledger result; it does not certify the economic value, legal status or editorial truth of an attached document. [1]

The public XRPL reference describes Ledger validation as part of a larger transaction or ledger lifecycle. Read the associated field definitions and constraints together, rather than treating a single displayed value as complete evidence. The network, account, transaction hash and validated state provide the context needed to interpret the result. Documentation examples explain a format; they are not observations of the current state of a particular wallet. [1]

Author interpretation: preserve the evidence needed to explain Ledger validation to another reader and keep pending outcomes visible until they are resolved. Use the same meaning in customer messages and exported receipts. This recommendation follows the documented lifecycle and does not claim a fresh network experiment. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
